clue.text: Aware clubs are almost packed

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: almost means the word for packed loses its final letter

parts.note: packed means full

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the golf clubs are nearly crammed in.
explanation.definitionFit: Being careful means being watchful and alert, so it is a synonym of aware.

clue.text: Rogues steal shilling

parts.note: to creep is to steal along, moving stealthily
S is the abbreviation for the old British shilling coin

explanation.surface: Villains pinch a small coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steal' means move stealthily here, not rob. The shilling was a pre-decimal British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Creeps are unpleasant, contemptible people, close to rogues.

clue.text: Consider wine, eating fish

indicators.note: eating means the wine piece takes the fish inside it

parts.note: red is a kind of wine
a gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: Someone ponders red wine with a fish course.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something is to look at or think about it, a synonym of consider.

clue.text: Craft is for green aliens

indicators.note: craft as a verb means to fashion, so the letters of is for green are shaped anew

explanation.surface: A spaceship is for little green men from another planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' reads as a spaceship but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliens in the legal sense are people from another country.

clue.text: Wants trousers but no top

indicators.note: but no top means the word for trousers loses its first letter in this down clue

parts.note: slacks are casual trousers

explanation.surface: Someone wants trousers but not a shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Wants in its older sense means is without or needs, a synonym.

clue.text: Profit for returning salesmen

parts.note: pro means in favour of, i.e. for

indicators.note: returning means the word for salesmen is read backwards

parts.note: reps are sales representatives

explanation.surface: Travelling salesmen coming back bring in money.
explanation.definitionFit: To profit, as a verb, is to do well or thrive, a synonym.

clue.text: Favourite job? Er … producing oil

parts.note: a pet is a favourite
a role is a job or function
um, like er, is a hesitation sound

explanation.surface: Someone dithers over their ideal job before naming oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude mineral oil extracted from the ground is this substance.

clue.text: Writer initially lost following old motorway sign

indicators.note: following means the trimmed writer comes after old and motorway

parts.note: M designates a British motorway, as in the M1

indicators.note: initially lost means the word for writer drops its first letter

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A writer got lost after an old motorway sign.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign or portent of future events.

clue.text: Shares drink with son after no one turned up

indicators.note: after means the son comes behind the reversed piece

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the words no and one are read upwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A drink is shared with a son after nobody arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Portions are parts or helpings, synonymous with shares.

clue.text: Liberated doctor lived here having left hospital

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged
having left means the hospital letter departs from the word here

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A freed medic once lived here after leaving hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having left' takes H out of HERE to leave ERE; 'doctor' rearranges LIVED with ERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Relieved can mean freed from a burden or duty, so close to liberated.

clue.text: Anxious period guarding the Queen? On the contrary

indicators.note: guarding signals one piece wrapped round another
on the contrary says the guarding works the other way round: the queen's letters wrap the period

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A worried spell of time spent protecting the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, AGE would surround ER; 'On the contrary' flips it so ER surrounds AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious can mean keen to do something, as in anxious to please, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Place for Holy Communion had claret prepared

indicators.note: prepared suggests the letters of the words had claret being made ready in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone got the wine ready for the communion service.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's principal church is where the Eucharist is regularly celebrated.

clue.text: Leave for each expedition

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person
a mission is an expedition sent for a purpose

explanation.surface: Time off granted for every journey undertaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave as a noun means consent, as in 'by your leave', a synonym.

clue.text: City name that is encapsulating 'charming' primarily

indicators.note: encapsulating means one piece encloses another, here the abbreviation for that is holds a letter

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for that is (id est)

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter of charming

explanation.surface: A city is described as being, in short, charming.
explanation.definitionFit: The resort on the French Riviera is a city in southern France.

clue.text: Criminal denied it if recognised

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong, so the letters of denied it if are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crook denied a crime even after being picked out.
explanation.definitionFit: To identify someone is to recognise who they are, so both are past participles.

clue.text: The state of being out of control?

definitions.text: The state of being out of control?

parts.words: The state of being out of control?
parts.note: being out of someone else's control is being free of rule, the condition a former colony achieves

explanation.surface: A description of chaos or anarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests disorder; read cryptically it is a nation no longer controlled by another.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-government, free of outside rule, is exactly the condition of not being under another's control.

clue.text: Kill time and give orders heartlessly

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: heartlessly means the word for give orders loses its central letter

parts.note: to dictate is to give orders

explanation.surface: A ruthless tyrant spends time ordering killings.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to wipe out or destroy completely, close to kill.

clue.text: Guaranteed to take off last chunky skirt

indicators.note: to take off last means the word for guaranteed drops its final letter

parts.note: sure means certain or guaranteed
round, of a figure, means plump or chunky

explanation.surface: A chunky skirt is certain to be the last garment shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirt' looks like a garment noun but is the verb, to go round the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: To skirt something is to go around its edge, so encircle or enclose it.

clue.text: A trip's bringing in five loans

indicators.note: bringing in means the dance piece takes the five letter inside it

parts.note: trip's is read as trip is, and to trip is to dance lightly
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A holiday involves taking out five loans.
explanation.definitionFit: Advances are sums of money paid ahead, that is loans.

clue.text: Gran turned me off thong?

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters of gran turned me are rearranged

explanation.surface: Granny was put off by a skimpy piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'off' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is one example of an item worn beneath outer clothes, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Admit defeat: I have to cut alcohol

indicators.note: to cut means the abbreviated I have splits the alcohol word

parts.note: gin is an alcoholic spirit
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone concedes they have to reduce their drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: To give in is to surrender or concede defeat.

clue.text: A student wearing earring upset grown-ups

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the combination is turned upside down
wearing means the earring word takes on the student letter as if putting it on

parts.note: a stud is a kind of earring
L is the learner driver's letter, standing for student

explanation.surface: A student with a stud in their ear annoys the grown-ups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts L inside STUD giving STLUD; 'upset' reverses that to DULTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Adults are fully grown people, a synonym of grown-ups.

clue.text: Proper piece of fishing equipment, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means the word is heard rather than seen, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: a reel winds the line on a fishing rod

explanation.surface: Someone is told about a genuine item of angling gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Real means genuine or proper, as in a real gentleman.

clue.text: If PM lied, is having a reshuffle made more understandable?

indicators.note: a reshuffle is a rearrangement, so the letters of if PM lied is are reordered

explanation.surface: Would a lying Prime Minister reshuffling the cabinet make politics clearer?
explanation.walkthrough: A cabinet reshuffle is a prime minister's rearrangement of ministers, apt for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To simplify is to make plainer or easier to grasp, matching the definition in tense.

clue.text: Judy's husband's magazine

definitions.meaning: in the seaside ... and Judy puppet show, Judy is married to the hook-nosed puppet
a long-running British humour weekly bore this name

explanation.surface: A wife's partner has his own periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch and Judy is a traditional British seaside puppet show; Punch was also a British satirical magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name the same character and the satirical weekly named after him.

clue.text: Somewhat major carnivore

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the words major carnivore is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A description of a fairly large meat-eater.
explanation.definitionFit: The killer whale is a major predator, an apex carnivore of the seas.

clue.text: Not confident about following United Nations volunteers in Ireland

indicators.note: following means the letter for about comes after the United Nations abbreviation

parts.note: C, circa, means about

indicators.note: in means the volunteers' letters go inside the name for Ireland

parts.note: Erin is a poetic name for Ireland
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Someone unsure about United Nations volunteers serving in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncertain describes someone lacking assurance, a direct synonym of not confident.

clue.text: Perfect international trade

parts.note: a deal is a trade or transaction

explanation.surface: A flawless global commercial agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means flawless, a synonym of perfect.

clue.text: Fail to take on board marine's complaint

indicators.note: take on board means hold inside, like cargo on a ship, so the marine piece goes within

parts.note: to die is to fail, as an engine dies
marine gives sea, with the possessive s added

explanation.surface: A sailor grumbles about failing to grasp something.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in medicine is an illness or ailment.

clue.text: Thrashings concealed by popular heads of grammar schools

parts.note: hid means concealed
in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: heads of means take the first letters of grammar and schools

explanation.surface: Head teachers at grammar schools once handed out beatings.
explanation.walkthrough: Grammar schools are selective state secondary schools in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiding is a beating, so the plural matches thrashings.
